Growing-Season Monthly Mixed-Effects Model Experiment

Generated: 2026-08-20

Experiment: the established all-events mixed-effects framework is applied separately to June, July, August, and September. A common balanced bootstrap sample size is used within each response so model performance is comparable among months.
Key findings: Full-model runoff-occurrence AUC was highest in September (0.973). Perennial crop fraction showed its clearest monthly role in August: the standardized occurrence coefficient was -0.70 (95% CI -1.10 to -0.30; p<0.001), and removing it increased AIC by 12.14 on average, with p<0.05 in 96% of bootstrap comparisons. No monthly perennial-fraction effect was supported for runoff magnitude.

Model definitions

Runoff occurrence is analyzed with a Mixed-effects logistic model. Runoff magnitude is defined as log(RC) and analyzed with a Mixed-effects linear regression model. Every model includes a site random intercept.

Precipitation-characteristics include log 30-minute precipitation intensity and log seven-day antecedent precipitation. Frozen-soil condition is not estimable in June-September because all retained events are non-frozen. Agricultural management includes growing-season tillage passes and current-water-year perennial crop fraction. Physical site properties include mean slope, soil infiltration group, and site-level tile drainage.

Crop residue is not included during the growing season, consistent with the established seasonal models.

Changing role of vegetation

Perennial crop fraction is the available event-level vegetation indicator. Its role is evaluated using drop-one model support, standardized Full-model coefficients, and marginal response curves.

Output files

Every figure is saved in PNG and PDF format. Bootstrap results, final coefficients, specifications, vegetation summaries, and marginal predictions are saved as CSV files under 04_Results/Mixed_Effects_Monthly_Growing_Season/Tables. Final fitted models are saved as RDS files.
